open_points.subject: Python runtime identity
open_points.text: Installing the release fails when the digest differs for any one dependency of each kind rule 1 names — a direct Python package, a transitive one, the Python version and the base image — and no instance of that release starts.
open_points.question: Does the Python runtime have a digest, and if so, what artifact does that digest identify; or must this test vary the exact Python version instead?
options: Python is identified only by its exact version, so the test changes that version.
Python has both an exact version and a digest of a specified runtime artifact.
Python is fixed indirectly by the base-image digest, so there is no separate Python digest check.
open_points.default_guess: Identify Python by exact version and test a version mismatch; use digests only for package distribution files and the base image.

witness.initial: The release lists Python 3.13 and the installer provides Python 3.13 from a different build.
events: The release process checks the installed Python runtime.
The installer attempts to start Registry.
outcomes: Installation is accepted because the exact Python version matches and no separate Python digest exists.
Installation is refused because the Python build has a different digest.

open_points.subject: digest-mismatch test coverage
open_points.text: the digest differs for any one dependency of each kind rule 1 names
open_points.question: Must the test alter every individual dependency in turn, one arbitrary dependency from each kind, or one representative fixture for each kind?
options: Test every listed dependency independently.
Test one arbitrarily selected dependency of every kind for each release.
Use one fixed representative fixture for each kind.
open_points.default_guess: Test one mutation for every dependency entry, plus the Python and base-image cases.

witness.initial: A release contains two direct packages and three transitive packages.
events: The test suite changes only one direct and one transitive package digest.
A defect accepts a changed digest for another transitive package.
outcomes: The suite passes because one dependency of each kind was tested.
The suite fails its coverage requirement because every dependency had to be tested.

open_points.subject: invalid release disposition
open_points.text: A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, or names one without an exact version or a digest, is not made.
open_points.question: What required outcome does “is not made” denote: no build artifact, no admitted/published release, or merely a release that cannot be installed?
options: The build produces no release artifact.
An artifact may be built but cannot be admitted or published as a release.
A release may exist but every installation of it is refused.
open_points.default_guess: The candidate may be built for diagnosis but is not admitted or published as a release.

witness.initial: A build produces an artifact whose dependency list omits an imported package.
events: The build system detects the omission after packaging.
An operator looks for or attempts to install the candidate.
outcomes: No release artifact exists.
An artifact exists, but it is marked inadmissible and cannot be installed.

open_points.subject: failed-installation start boundary
open_points.text: and no instance of that release starts.
open_points.question: At what observable boundary has an instance “started”: process creation, opening any listener, becoming ready, or answering a request?
options: No Registry process is created.
A process may run validation but opens no listener.
A listener may open, but the instance never becomes ready or answers requests.
open_points.default_guess: Permit preflight validation processes, but open no Registry listener and serve no request.

witness.initial: An installation has a mismatched package digest.
events: The installer launches Registry in validation mode.
Registry detects the mismatch before marking itself ready.
outcomes: The guarantee is broken because a Registry process started.
The guarantee holds because no listener opened and no instance became ready.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and monitoring system

open_points.subject: scope of exact running dependencies
open_points.text: the dependencies the running instance has are exactly the release's list, by name, version and digest, nothing more.
open_points.question: Does “nothing more” quantify only over the dependency kinds in rule 1, or also over host facilities such as the kernel, firmware, mounted certificates, runtime-injected libraries and installation tooling?
options: Only Python packages, the Python runtime and the base image are compared.
Every executable or library reachable by the process is a dependency.
All runtime inputs, including host-provided facilities and mounted data, must be listed.
open_points.default_guess: Limit the equality to rule 1's closed categories: Python packages, Python version and base image.

witness.initial: The listed packages, Python version and base image match, but the host supplies its kernel and a mounted CA bundle.
events: The exact-dependency test inventories its environment.
outcomes: The test passes because host facilities are outside rule 1's dependency categories.
The test fails because the running instance has unlisted runtime dependencies.

open_points.subject: release identity and immutability
open_points.text: the same release installed again gives the same list.
open_points.question: What makes two installations the “same release,” and may a release identifier or version label ever be rebound to different artifacts?
options: The release version string is the identity and is permanently immutable.
The release artifact's digest is the identity; labels may move.
A source revision plus build configuration identifies the release.
open_points.default_guess: Use an immutable release-artifact digest, with a version label that may never be rebound.

witness.initial: Version 1.4.0 was installed once; a rebuilt artifact with different transitive dependencies is later published under the same version label.
events: The dependency list is compared with the first installation.
outcomes: It is the same release and must be refused because its dependency list changed.
It is a new release because its artifact digest differs, despite sharing the label.

open_points.subject: release dependency-list contract
open_points.question: What exact representation and equality rules will the release and installer use for package, Python and base-image entries, including digest algorithm, distribution choice and normalization?
options: Use one uniform name/version/digest record for every kind.
Use typed entries: package distribution name/version/file digest, Python exact version or runtime digest, and OCI image digest.
Compare an immutable lockfile and image manifest as opaque signed artifacts.
open_points.default_guess: Use typed entries and SHA-256-style algorithm-qualified digests over the exact package distribution files and OCI image manifest.
consequences: A uniform record is simple but invents potentially meaningless name, version or digest fields for Python and images.
Typed entries preserve each dependency kind's identity but require kind-specific comparison rules.
Opaque manifest comparison is strong but makes individual mismatch diagnostics and the required per-kind tests harder.
open_points.requirement: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system libraries and the store's engine.

witness.initial: A package name and version are unchanged, but the release uses a different wheel for another platform; the image tag is unchanged but its manifest digest moved.
events: The deploy tooling compares the release list with the installed environment.
outcomes: Comparison passes after normalizing only names and versions.
Comparison fails because the exact distribution-file and image-manifest digests differ.

open_points.subject: dependency completeness proof
open_points.text: misses a package the instance would import
open_points.question: How will the release process establish the complete direct and transitive package closure, especially for conditional imports, entry points and packages loaded only on uncommon execution paths?
options: Derive the closure from a fully resolved locked dependency graph.
Observe imports while executing a prescribed workload.
Combine the resolved graph with static and runtime checks.
open_points.default_guess: Use the fully resolved locked graph as the authoritative closure and supplement it with import checks.
consequences: A locked graph covers unexecuted paths but may include packages that are never loaded.
Runtime observation reflects one execution but can miss conditional paths.
Combined checks are broader but require reconciliation when the graph and observed imports differ.
open_points.requirement: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system libraries and the store's engine.

open_points.subject: missing non-package dependency fields
open_points.text: A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, or names one without an exact version or a digest, is not made.
open_points.question: Must this refusal test also show rejection when the Python version or base-image entry is absent, when the Python version is not exact, or when the base-image digest is absent?
options: Yes; omission and incomplete identity must be tested for every dependency kind in rule 1.
No; item 2 covers packages only, and item 3 proves the other kinds indirectly.
Python and base-image omissions belong only to installation tests, not release-creation tests.
open_points.default_guess: Add explicit omission and incomplete-identity cases for Python and the base image as well as packages.

witness.initial: A candidate release lists every package but omits the base-image entry.
events: The release process evaluates Required test 2.
The candidate is offered for installation.
outcomes: The candidate is made because test 2 speaks only of a missing package.
The candidate is refused because every dependency kind named by rule 1 must be present.

open_points.subject: dependencies security-review reopening
open_points.text: Performed again on 2026-11-24, after A20 rule 5 recorded that its rules are kept by the release process and its installation, outside Registry (owner), and A20 declared no formal invariant of Registry's code. No rule of what a release contains or how it is installed moved.
open_points.question: Has the dependencies category been reviewed again after the present change to A20's Required tests, as A21 rule 2 requires, and what is the recorded outcome of that review?
options: Reopen A21 now, review the new A20 tests, and record the new performance with its outcome.
Declare explicitly that changing Required tests is not a change to a decision for rule 2.
Broaden the existing 2026-11-24 review record so it expressly covers the current A20 test change.
open_points.default_guess: Reopen the dependencies review and add a new performed-again record stating whether the outcome changed.

witness.initial: A21's latest recorded A20 review covers rule 5 and the absence of Registry invariants; A20's Required tests are then replaced by four broader tests.
events: A21 rule 2 is applied to the changed A20 decision.
The security review is presented as complete.
outcomes: The dependencies category is reopened because a named decision changed.
The review remains closed because no normative rule changed.

open_points.subject: dependencies category affected scope
open_points.text: dependencies: APPLICABLE; references: A20; affected: Registry release, its Python dependencies
open_points.question: Does this category's affected scope include the Python runtime, the base image, its system libraries and the store engine, or only Python packages?
options: Expand the affected list to every dependency kind A20 names.
Treat “Python dependencies” as an umbrella that includes the Python runtime and base image.
Keep the affected list package-only, leaving the other A20 dependency kinds outside this category.
open_points.default_guess: Expand the affected list expressly to Python packages, Python runtime, base image, system libraries and store engine.

witness.initial: All package digests are correct, but the installed base image has a different digest.
events: The dependencies security review determines whether the case is within its affected scope.
outcomes: The mismatch is within the reviewed category because A20 is referenced as a whole.
The mismatch is outside the stated affected scope because only Python dependencies are named.

open_points.subject: A21 test aggregation for external release tests
open_points.text: Each APPLICABLE category's decisions have their own required tests, and those tests pass.
open_points.question: Which later gate establishes this A21 item for A20 now that A20's tests run in the release process rather than in Registry or `tools/design_lint.py`?
options: The factory gate consumes release-process test results before admitting a release.
Deployment runs A20's tests and supplies an attestation to the factory.
A21's design check verifies only that A20 declares tests, leaving their execution to deployment.
open_points.default_guess: Require factory admission to consume a successful, release-specific result from the release-process tests.
consequences: Factory aggregation gives one admission decision but couples it to external release tooling.
Deployment attestation keeps installation knowledge in deploy but requires a trusted handoff.
Checking only test declarations cannot demonstrate A21's phrase “those tests pass.”
open_points.requirement: Each APPLICABLE category's decisions have their own required tests, and those tests pass.
